newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Engine problems to cost Cathay $120-$150m.
newsitem.headline: Engine problems to cost Cathay $120-$150m.

text.p: Cancelled flights caused by engine problems on Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd's Airbus fleet are likely to pare HK$120 million to $150 million from the bottom line this year, chairman Peter Sutch said on Saturday.
Cathay Pacific and its 25.5 percent-owned Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) grounded their fleet of Airbus normal flight services.
"That is my best estimate of the impact on the bottom line as at this stage pre any form of discussion with the suppliers for inconvenience caused," Sutch told reporters.
Cathay has 11 A330-300 aircraft and Dragonair has four.
"We would expect to see the fleet ... back in service again within a couple of weeks," Sutch said.
The groundings followed a failure of a Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engine on a Dragonair flight, forcing the plane to make a single-engine landing in the Philippines.
It was the fifth time since November that a Cathay Pacific or Dragonair A330-300 had made a single-engine landing. Rolls-Royce said gearbox bearings were to blame.
The gearboxes are supplied by France's Hispano Suiza.
